program_overview.title: Frontend Development for Teens
program_overview.tagline: The frontend course with a design soul: CSS mastered as a craft, interfaces that feel expensive, and React learned as a UI instrument.
program_overview.description:
Every interface a teen admires, the smooth landing page, the app that feels expensive, is frontend craft, and craft is exactly what most courses skip on the way to frameworks. This live online course for ages 13 to 18 takes the design-forward road: HTML and CSS mastered properly, flexbox, grid, responsive discipline, then the styling craft layer, modern CSS, SASS architecture, Tailwind, and animations that make pages feel alive, on real JavaScript foundations. React arrives as a UI instrument: components, hooks, styling strategies and a design system built by the student. The final month adds accessibility and performance, the two marks of professional frontend, and ships a capstone with genuine polish.

This course pairs with our React for Teens course rather than repeating it: React for Teens goes deeper into application logic and TypeScript; this course goes deeper into the visual craft, CSS depth, animation, design systems, that makes interfaces worth using. Ambitious students take both roads over time.

The pace is honest: nine months at two live classes a week plus three to four hours of practice, with two more months in hand. Homework, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest. Real craft, real interfaces, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: CSS as a craft, not a chore: modern CSS, SASS architecture, Tailwind and animation get real weeks
Design systems built, not mentioned: the student ships a component library of their own
Accessibility and performance as the finishing school: the two marks of professional frontend
React taught as a UI instrument, complementing (not repeating) our React for Teens course
Everything deploys: public URLs from the first phase
Real assessment: weekly homework, monthly mixed reviews, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with a free retest

faqs.question: What will my teen build in this frontend course?
faqs.answer: More than 20 deployed interfaces across nine months: styled responsive pages, API-powered widgets, Tailwind builds, animated component sets, React UI projects, a personal design system with tokens and documentation, and a polished capstone interface presented at demo day. The visual craft is the point: work that visibly looks better than average.

faqs.question: How is this different from your React for Teens course?
faqs.answer: They are two halves of frontend, deliberately split. React for Teens goes deeper into application logic: state, TypeScript, data patterns and a product capstone. This course goes deeper into the visual craft: CSS mastery, SASS architecture, Tailwind, animation, design systems, accessibility and performance. Ambitious students take both roads over time; either order works.

faqs.question: How long does it take, and how is my teen assessed?
faqs.answer: Nine months at 2 live classes a week plus 3 to 4 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for students who need them. Homework follows every class, monthly assignments mix new questions with earlier topics, each phase ends with an exam, and a final exam, practical plus written, decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision.

faqs.question: Does this course cover Vue, Angular or Svelte?
faqs.answer: Honestly, no: framework tours produce students fluent in nothing. The craft taught here, CSS depth, component thinking, design systems, transfers to every framework in days, and React is included as the industry default UI instrument. A teen who owns this material picks up any alternative framework when a real project demands it.

faqs.question: Is frontend still a good skill in the AI era?
faqs.answer: More than ever, and specifically the craft half: AI tools generate average-looking interfaces in seconds, which makes above-average taste the differentiator. Judgment about spacing, motion, hierarchy and accessibility is exactly what this course trains, and exactly what tools cannot fake.
